newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Star Mining preferred bidder in Sukhoi Log gold.
newsitem.headline: Star Mining preferred bidder in Sukhoi Log gold.

text.p: Star Mining Corporation of Australia is the preferred bidder in a planned tender of shares in a unit of Russian miner Lenzoloto that will tap Russia's huge Sukhoi Log gold field, a Lenzoloto official said on Thursday.

"Star Mining enjoys the status of privileged bidder in the tender, since it is already our partner and has already invested in us," said Alexei Mikhailov, secretary of the board of directors of Lenzoloto.
Mikhailov said Lenzoloto had been working with Star Mining unit Star Technology Systems, but he said that the parent company, not the unit, would bid in the tender.
He said Star Mining, which nominally holds a 31 percent stake in Lenzoloto, had already invested $50 million in the Russian company.

The aide to First Deputy Natural Resources Minister Boris Yatskevich, who is also Lenzoloto's board chairman, said earlier on Thursday that a 49 percent stake in joint-stock company Sukhoi Log, a unit of Lenzoloto, would be offered in March.

Mikhailov said total investment needed to reach and sustain peak production at the southeast Siberian gold field was $1.5 billion over an unspecified period of time, and gave the following broad terms of the tender.
He said the tender winner would be required to pay a $60 million signing bonus, $200 million for the equity stake and provde $500 million in bank-guaranteed financing.
Other tender details would be worked out at a Lenzoloto board meeting at a later date.

Mikhailov said that Sukhoi Log -- the largest gold field in the former Soviet Union and possibly one of the biggest in the world, with 1,100 tonnes (about 35 million troy ounces) -- would not be exploited on a production-sharing basis.
The field contained possibly as much platinum, not palladium, as gold, he said, but he said there did not exist a suitable technology to extract the platinum.
Lenzoloto would be the vendor of a 49 percent stake in Lenzoloto unit joint-stock company Sukhoi Log, which will tap the eponymous gold field, he said.
He said the exact tender date, pegged in March by a Natural Resources Ministry aide, had to be confirmed by the board.
